title: Alerting and on-call: the defect that only shows up with real users

videos.script: Lesson one wrote down a promise. When the error rate passes two percent, the person on call knows within five minutes. {{promise}} This is the lesson that keeps it. {{keep}} Some defects only exist with real users. A payment provider that fails on a Friday night. A thousand people on one page. {{real}} No test before the release could have caught them. So something has to notice, and wake the right person. {{notice}} You will write the alert as a rule, and then test the rule, with numbers you invent. {{rule}} Then you will watch it fire for real, against a box office whose payments fail one time in three. {{firing}} And you will see the alert that fired and reached nobody, which is a common way for alerting to fail. {{nobody}} After that, the people. Who is on call, what the runbook says, and how a team writes about an incident without blaming anyone. {{people}} And at the end, what the four parts of this course had in common all along. {{end}}
